comparison: Both affirm the methodological rigor of data collection and processing (C1-C3, C20-C21, C28, C34, C42-C43, C45-C47, C135-C136). OpenEval provides detailed technical validation of specific tools and methods, while peer reviewers emphasize overall reproducibility and thoroughness. Peer review also includes gender/name prediction methods (C49, C57) and code availability (C148-C158) in their methodological assessment, which OpenEval evaluates separately.

Perfect agreement on gender representation trends (C4, C22-C23, C64, C66-C67). Both confirm the temporal improvement in female representation and the specific 2017-2018 shift. OpenEval provides detailed technical analysis of the trend, while peer reviewers explicitly state the evidence is 'convincing' and accept the findings without challenge.

Complete agreement on the key finding that quote trends improved faster than authorship proportions (C5, C102). OpenEval emphasizes this as a positive trend in journalism practices, while peer reviewers implicitly accept it as part of the overall gender analysis with 'more nuanced' interpretation in the revised version.

Both support the article-type-specific findings (C6, C24, C71-C72). OpenEval provides detailed quantitative validation and discusses the recommendation implications (C162-C163), while peer reviewers accept these findings as well-presented and contextualized without specific challenge.

Strong agreement on the major finding of East Asian under-representation (C7-C8, C103). OpenEval validates the novelty claim (C25) and provides extensive quantitative support (C80-C81, C84, C87-C90), while peer reviewers explicitly confirm the evidence is 'convincing' and accept this as a key contribution presenting 'compelling answers.'

Both address citation patterns and their comparison to quote patterns (C77-C79, C82-C83, C85-C86). OpenEval notes these are less disparate than quotes and provides nuanced analysis of first vs. last author differences. Peer review implicitly accepts these findings as part of the rigorous analysis, with one reviewer noting the distinction between citations and quotes (C174) is well-supported.

Both support the mechanistic insight about where disparities arise (C92-C93, C159). OpenEval emphasizes the comparison between all quotes and cited-only quotes as revealing the journalistic process. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this inference as part of the nuanced interpretation, though OpenEval notes the causal inference is reasonable but not definitively proven.

Strong agreement on journalist name origin patterns (C94-C96). OpenEval provides detailed validation while noting potential confounding factors and sample size limitations. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the technically competent analysis with improved legibility, and the recommendation about journalist influence (C178) is supported.

Both affirm the appropriate acknowledgment of methodological limitations (C105-C109, C50). OpenEval emphasizes the thoroughness and scientific caution of the limitations discussion. Peer reviewers explicitly state 'caveats are inevitable' while maintaining evidence is 'convincing,' and one reviewer finds the approach 'certainly adequate' despite broad caveats.

Strong agreement on fundamental study limitations (C115-C120). OpenEval validates that the study measures visibility rather than complete journalistic process. Peer reviewers explicitly address these limitations, noting 'Broad caveats remain about the nature of authorship' but concluding the approach is 'certainly adequate.' Both also accept limitations about comparator datasets (C121, C126-C128).

Both support authorship position findings (C61-C63, C65, C69-C70) and career stage patterns (C97-C99, C167-C169). OpenEval provides detailed validation of stable authorship proportions contrasted with changing quotes. Peer reviewers explicitly note authors 'did well to incorporate discussion of authorship and the scholarly division of labour,' accepting these findings as appropriately contextualized.

Complete agreement on code and data availability supporting reproducibility (C152-C158). OpenEval emphasizes this represents best practices in computational reproducibility with detailed technical validation. Peer reviewers explicitly confirm the analysis is 'importantly, reproducible' and 'the authors provide the code and data for reproduction.'

Both support the statistical methods for confidence intervals (C148-C151). OpenEval validates bootstrap methods as appropriate with adequate sample size. Peer reviewers implicitly accept these methods as part of the overall rigorous and reproducible methodology without specific challenge.

OpenEval validates gender prediction methodology with detailed technical assessment (C49-C56, C185-C186), including error rates and limitations. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the overall methodological rigor but do not provide specific evaluation of gender prediction methods separately from general methodology.

OpenEval validates name origin prediction methodology (C57-C60, C73-C74, C144-C147) with emphasis on probability assignments and conceptual clarity. Peer reviewers accept this as part of the rigorous methodology but do not separately evaluate name origin prediction methods.

Both support claims about generalizability and reproducibility (C25-C27, C111, C114). OpenEval validates novelty claims and software generalizability. Peer reviewers emphasize reproducibility and implicitly support potential for extension to other outlets, with one noting the paper 'will be of interest to science journalists.'

Overlap on recommendations and impact (C27, C111, C114). OpenEval validates citations about awareness reducing bias and available resources. Peer reviewers accept recommendations as reasonable implications, noting 'the discussion is richer, the interpretation of the results is more nuanced.'

Both support conceptual framing and recommendations (C9-C10, C18-C19, C131-C134). OpenEval validates journalism's role and bias propagation mechanisms with literature support. Peer reviewers implicitly accept recommendations as well-contextualized, with the editor noting the paper will be of interest to journalists.

Both support recommendations for region-specific journalists and other interventions (C172-C178, C182). OpenEval connects findings to prior literature and validates proposed mechanisms. Peer reviewers accept these as reasonable implications without challenge, noting improved contextualization.

Both address limitations in comparator datasets (C126-C128). OpenEval identifies the unvalidated assumption that newsworthy papers match all papers demographically as a significant limitation. Peer reviewers acknowledge 'Broad caveats remain' about authorship and expectations for who should be quoted, finding the approach 'certainly adequate.'

Both support recommendations for extending the work (C129-C130). OpenEval validates these as reasonable future directions. Peer reviewers implicitly support generalizability through emphasis on reproducibility and methodological rigor.

Both address generalizability beyond Nature (C121-C125). OpenEval notes the preliminary Guardian analysis and lack of clear comparators as limiting interpretation. Peer reviewers emphasize reproducibility supports extension to other outlets, implicitly accepting these limitations.

Both support recommendations for multi-outlet geographic analysis (C179-C181). OpenEval acknowledges inability to robustly analyze geographic patterns as an honest limitation. Peer reviewers implicitly accept this through emphasis on reproducibility enabling future extensions.

Both address temporal trends and career stage patterns (C97-C99). OpenEval validates the concerning temporal divergence while noting projections about future impacts are speculative. Peer reviewers accept these findings as part of the authorship discussion that was 'well incorporated.'

Both support nuanced temporal and career-stage analysis (C164-C171, C167-C169). OpenEval validates data-driven time periods and thoughtful interpretation. Peer reviewers accept the discussion of authorship conventions and diversity by career stage as well-incorporated.

OpenEval validates extension of quote findings to mentions (C160-C161), noting consistency strengthens overall findings. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers accepted overall findings without separately evaluating mentions analysis.

OpenEval validates appropriate contextualization from prior literature (C11-C17), including baseline expectations and methodological choices. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers accepted overall rigor without separately evaluating literature context.

OpenEval validates detailed article type descriptions and temporal patterns (C29-C41). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers accepted overall methodology without separately evaluating article type classifications.

OpenEval validates detailed data processing steps with clear rationales (C137-C143, C183-C184). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers accepted overall methodology as rigorous without separately evaluating specific processing steps.

OpenEval validates choice of Springer Nature comparator and sampling approach (C187-C191). No corresponding peer review evaluation found; peer reviewers accepted overall methodology without separately evaluating comparator selection rationale.
